acceptance: Baseline file(s) are tracked at a documented path and cover only static (`--no-llm`) findings.

Every baseline entry has a specific reason naming why the finding is a false positive or declared purpose; no entry keeps the auto-generated default reason (`rg 'auto-generated baseline'` over the baseline finds nothing).
Scanning every tracked skill with `--no-llm --baseline <file> --fail-on-findings` exits 0.
Negative check: the same scan without the baseline reports exactly the findings the baseline lists, no more and no fewer (counts match per skill).
No baseline entry suppresses a finding triaged as real.
context: Batch: skillspector-remediation (serial mode; this repository names no prepared-delivery policy). All catalog work lands on branch chore/retire-tidy-perms, worktree ~/Developer/skill-sync-skills.wt-retire-tidy-perms, in the one final PR #118. Owner decisions (2026-11-13) are recorded in ~/.agents/handoffs/skill-sync-skills-skillspector-remediation-20261113.md. Scanner: NVIDIA SkillSpector v2.12.0 at commit 9dc82fe473329b2b742aa5097dcfe7ae55f51b01. Close each item only after PR #118 has actually merged, unless the item says otherwise. Guardrails: never `git add -A`; stage explicit paths. Commit as the human author in ~/.gitconfig, no agent co-author trailer. No push to main and no history rewrite. Do not reword skill prose to dodge a keyword rule. Do not touch files outside this item's scope; report adjacent issues instead. Run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` before each commit; a failure blocks the commit. Decision gates: (1) Test whether `skillspector scan --recursive` accepts `--baseline`. If yes, use one baseline for skills/; if not, use one baseline per affected skill and a per-skill loop. Record which. (2) If the baseline matches by line number or content fingerprint, note in README how to regenerate it after a legitimate edit to a flagged line. (3) A new static finding that appears since the first scan must be triaged before it is baselined. Guardrail: never baseline by rule ID or whole file if the format allows a narrower match. Expected static findings: todo AS1 references/bootstrap.md:65 and RA2 references/queries.md:21; shared-agent-execution EA2 x2 references/external-harnesses.md:115; code EA2 references/pr-sweep.md:26; shared-investigation-framework EA2 SKILL.md:83. Out of scope: the skill-sync AS3 finding (owned by ~/Developer/skill-sync).

description: After the tidy-perms removal, the static scan reports 6 findings (two of them the same line) across todo, shared-agent-execution, code and shared-investigation-framework. All were triaged as false positives or declared purpose. Without a baseline a CI gate fails on its first run; rewording the flagged guardrail sentences to satisfy keyword rules would weaken them. Owner decision: commit a baseline that suppresses exactly these findings, each with its own written reason. Baselines are generated with `skillspector baseline --no-llm`, then the generic reason is replaced per finding.
